Let's analyze each:

Option A: "The products of protein digestion may be absorbed as free amino acids or as di- or tripeptides." This seems plausible: after digestion, proteins are broken into peptides; some can be absorbed as free amino acids or intact oligopeptides. Peptide absorption occurs in brush border where peptidases break down to di- and tripeptides? I'm not entirely sure. Typically, small peptides (<10 aa) may be absorbed as oligopeptides; but the main route is free amino acids. Option A says "may be" which allows possibility. So it's likely true.

Option B: "Protein digestion and absorption does not involve any brush-border enzymes." That's false because brush border peptidases (like dipeptidyl peptidase, etc.) do break down peptides into absorbable units. So B is incorrect.

Option C: "Protein digestion only takes place in the stomach." False; protein digestion also occurs in duodenum via pancreatic enzymes and brush border. So C false.

Option D: "The products of digestion of dietary protein by luminal and brush-border enzymes are only absorbed by one of the 14 different amino acid transporters." That seems too restrictive: there are many transporters for various amino acids, not just one. And also peptides may use specific transporters; but I think it's false.

Option E: "Gastric digestion of all proteins is equally efficient because of the grinding action of the antrum." This is nonsense: gastric digestion varies by protein type and enzyme secretion; antrum does grind but not equal for all. So false.

Option H: "Gastric digestion of all proteins is less efficient due to the grinding action of the antrum." Grinding occurs in stomach? Option J: "The products of protein digestion are only absorbed as di- or tripeptides." That's too restrictive; they can be free amino acids. So false.

First, recall facts about the UK constitution. The United Kingdom has no single written constitution; it's uncodified.
